messages.subject: Working with legends [newbie]
parts:
Hi,

I have plotted two lines in the same graphic using the following code:

qplot( month, tau, data = top10, geom = "line" ) +
geom_line( data = top100, linetype = "dashed" )

I have also tried to add labels for each line to be included in a side
legend but without success.

What is the best way to define a label for each line and print these
in a side box ?

Also, how can I change the linetype of the first line, the one defined
in the qplot command? It is always "solid".

Thanks in advance,
--
Sérgio Nunes

messages.subject: Re: Working with legends [newbie]

Thanks.

Given that my data has no "facet" column - just x and y (no "f").
What is the best way to add a column "f" with value "v1" to a given data frame ?

Can this be done on the fly with ggplot2, i.e. without altering the
original data frame ?

--
Sérgio Nunes



2009/11/19 baptiste auguie <bapt...@googlemail.com>:
> Hi,
>
> It's hard to tell what you want without the data, but the general idea
> is to specify a mapping between the geom (a line here) and an
> aesthetic parameter (colour, or linetype, etc.).
>
> Consider the following example,
>
> d1 <- data.frame(x=1:10, y=rnorm(10), f="a")
> d2 <- data.frame(x=1:10, y=rnorm(10), f="b")
>
> p =
> qplot( x, y, data = d1, geom = "line", linetype=f) +
> geom_line( data = d2, mapping=aes(linetype=f))
>
> p
>
> The linetype is mapped to the variable "f", and is automatically added
> as a legend. You can specify manually what linetypes you want with,
>
>
> p + scale_linetype_manual("my legend", values=c("dotted", "dashed"))
>
> HTH,
>
> baptiste

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Working with legends [newbie]
parts:
> Given that my data has no "facet" column - just x and y (no "f").
> What is the best way to add a column "f" with value "v1" to a given data frame ?
>
> Can this be done on the fly with ggplot2, i.e. without altering the
> original data frame ?

Yes:

qplot( month, tau, data = top10, geom = "line", colour = "top10" ) +
geom_line(aes(colour = "top100") data = top100, linetype = "dashed" )

but it's a bit easier to see what's going on if you use ggplot()

ggplot(aes(month, tau)) +
geom_line(aes(colour = "top10"), data = top10) +
geom_line(aes(colour = "top100"), data = top100)
